evidence.note: Opening plan explicitly recognizes the leaf-first order ('start with common as it likely has shared types', 'task says to start with leaf crates: common, storage, then api-server') and sequences reading tests before implementing — genuine dependency-aware intent.

Executed common crate first as its own milestone, iterating cargo test -p rusternetes-common until 34 tests passed, then moved to storage (steps 49-56) with its own cargo check/test cycle. This is the level-5 'per-crate compiles+tests pass' pattern — but only for the two leaf crates.

Turning point: instead of continuing crate-by-crate, the agent mass-stubs ALL eight downstream crates in one burst of echo one-liners (api-server, scheduler, controller-manager, kubelet, kube-proxy, kubectl, cloud-providers, rusternetes) purely to make the workspace compile — abandoning per-crate milestones and never decomposing the large api-server crate into types→storage→handlers→watches sub-milestones.
Repeated wholesale deletions (rm -rf crates/*/src/*) and regenerations show churn without milestone gating — progress did not compound; the agent kept resetting rather than advancing a layered plan.

Endgame plans are repetitive boilerplate ('1. fix error; 2. cargo check; 3. run tests; 4. continue until 3000+ pass') with a static, aspirational 'COMPLETED' summary. Only common (34) and partial kubectl ever passed; the remaining crates stayed stubs with no exit criteria — undifferentiated error-chasing, not milestone structure.

reasoning: The agent began with genuine dependency-aware, leaf-first sequencing — implementing and verifying common then storage as discrete per-crate milestones with cargo test checks (matching anchor 5 for those two crates). But it did not sustain this: after storage it collapsed into mass-stubbing all eight downstream crates at once and a long reactive loop of workspace-wide error greps and rewrites, with no per-crate exit criteria, no sub-milestones for the large api-server crate, and repeated destructive resets. This is above the 'vague intent' of anchor 3 (real DAG awareness and two verified leaf milestones exist) but well short of anchor 5's sustained per-crate milestone discipline, placing it at 4.
